newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-HANDKERCHIEF PROTEST KEEPS SEVILLA PRESIDENT AWAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HANDKERCHIEF PROTEST KEEPS SEVILLA PRESIDENT AWAY.

text.p: The president of beleaguered Sevilla will no longer attend home games after several months in which angry fans greeted his arrival in the VIP box by waving white handkerchiefs.

A series of humiliating scandals have cost Jose Maria Gonzalez repeated 'panoladas' -- a traditional Spanish protest borrowed from bullfighting, which at times is also used to celebrate exceptional performances.
Gonzalez will also hand over the day-to-day running of the club to a deputy.
Sevilla are currently struggling fourth from bottom, but the disastrous season on the field has been more than matched by the poor run off it.
Amid various allegations, Sevilla have seen their reputation in the transfer market take a tumble and several players have complained publicly of not being paid.

Brazilian World Cup striker Bebeto joined the club for two months, before returning home saying he felt cheated. Several members of the board have openly mutinied against Gonzalez in a power struggle that goes back to the summer of 1995, when the club was reprieved from relegation to the third division because of accounting irregularities.
Sevilla's problems have contrasted with the runaway success of neighbours Real Betis, currently riding high in third place.
Sevilla coach Jose Antonio Camachao has already offered his resignation once this season, and is once again believed to be close to leaving the club.

"I'm the first to realise that ... if things are not sorted out, the club will take the measures it considers correct," said Camacho, who was in the running for the highly-prized Real Madrid job before joining Sevilla.
Camacho's side faces fifth-placed Real Sociedad this weekend, before travelling to fellow strugglers Zaragoza.
